message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**Apple's diluted EPS for fiscal 2024 (year ended September 28, 2024): $6.08** (down from $6.13 in FY2023; basic EPS $6.11).

**What I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and checked the live quote (last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72). The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales rose 2% to $391.0B, gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, operating income grew to $123.2B, and operating cash flow was a robust $118.3B, with $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Diluted EPS slipped to $6.08 from $6.13, but that decline was driven almost entirely by a one-time, non-cash-like $10.2B net income tax charge tied to the European Commission State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not by operating deterioration — pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B from $113.7B. Services revenue grew 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin, offsetting flat iPhone sales and an 8% decline in Greater China. Given the durable cash generation, expanding margins, and a price that is roughly flat versus the ~$222.86 average price at which Apple itself repurchased stock in September 2024, I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 — just above the ask, so it filled immediately at $222.75 for a total of $9,801. That is within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, uses only existing cash ($50,000 available), and involves no transfer of funds out of the account. I did not trade MSFT, and I placed no sell orders, consistent with the standing mandate.
